novel_features.name: Markdown to laid-out board
novel_features.description: Turn a Markdown file into native heading cards, rich-text notes, bullet lists and checkbox lists in evenly spaced columns.
novel_features.rationale: Builds Milanote's own heading, list and task nodes and computes canvas positions; every other tool drops plain cards into Unsorted.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this whenever a multi-section document has to land on a board looking organized, not one card at a time.

novel_features.name: Board tree to Markdown outline
novel_features.description: Get a board and its sub-boards back as Markdown in canvas reading order, with headings, lists and checkboxes intact.
novel_features.rationale: Orders cards by column and position and converts Milanote rich text to Markdown; Milanote's exporter only makes PDF and images.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it to read a whole board as text before editing or summarizing it.

novel_features.name: Even-grid re-space with undo
novel_features.description: Re-space a board's cards (or empty its Unsorted panel) onto an even grid with equal gutters, and undo it if you don't like it.
novel_features.rationale: Computes a grid from every element's position and applies it in one bulk move, keeping the old positions locally for undo.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it after edits to keep a board tidy without moving cards one by one.

novel_features.name: Storyboard and moodboard image grid
novel_features.description: Upload a folder of frames as an evenly spaced, numbered grid with optional captions.
novel_features.rationale: Uses each file's real pixel size to space the grid exactly and batches the uploads.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it for storyboards and reference boards instead of dropping images one at a time.

novel_features.name: Open tasks across all boards
novel_features.description: List every unchecked checkbox across your boards with where it lives, ready to tick off.
novel_features.rationale: A cross-board query over the local mirror; the web app has no such view.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it to answer what is left to do without opening every board.

novel_features.name: Layout lint
novel_features.description: Report off-grid cards, uneven gutters, overlaps, cards stuck in Unsorted, and text that should be a heading or list.
novel_features.rationale: Applies geometric and content rules across every element and returns findings with element ids.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it to verify a layout by numbers instead of a screenshot.

novel_features.name: Two-way Markdown sync
novel_features.description: Pair a Markdown file with a board so edits on either side flow to the other.
novel_features.rationale: Tracks which card came from which section and what changed since last run, so updates edit cards in place instead of duplicating them.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it when a document lives in both an editor and a board and must stay in step.

novel_features.name: Board snapshots and diff
novel_features.description: Save a board's state and later see exactly which cards were added, moved, edited or ticked.
novel_features.rationale: Keeps full element history locally; Milanote shows no change history.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it to review what changed between revisions without eyeballing the canvas.

novel_features.name: Board templates
novel_features.description: Save a board's structure as a small YAML kit and stamp out fresh copies.
novel_features.rationale: Serialises headings, columns, checklists and relative spacing, then rebuilds them with new ids.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it to start every project from the same organized layout.

novel_features.name: CSV to card grid
novel_features.description: Turn spreadsheet rows such as a shot list into a numbered, evenly spaced grid of cards.
novel_features.rationale: Maps columns to bold-labelled lines in native rich text and computes the grid.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it for tabular data instead of building cards one by one.

novel_features.name: One-command login from Chrome
novel_features.description: Pull the Milanote login from a running Chrome in one step.
novel_features.rationale: Reads only the Milanote session cookie over the DevTools protocol and stores it locally.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it to set up or refresh auth without exporting cookies by hand.

narrative.headline: Treat a Milanote board like an addressable canvas: native headings, lists and checkboxes, laid out on an even grid, and read back as Markdown.
narrative.value_prop: Every Milanote board, note, heading, to-do, image and comment from the command line, written through the same channel the web app uses. layout md turns a Markdown file into an evenly spaced board, outline turns a board back into Markdown, and a local mirror makes search and todos open work across every board offline.
narrative.auth_narrative: Milanote has no API keys. The CLI uses the session cookie from a browser where you are logged in. Easiest: start Chrome with remote debugging and run chrome-login, which copies only the Milanote session cookie. Or paste it with auth login --cookie, or point MILANOTE_COOKIE_FILE at a JSON cookie export. Sessions last about a month; doctor tells you when it has expired.

quickstart.comment: Check config and auth wiring without touching the network
Confirm the cookie works and find your root board id
Preview a Markdown file laid out as a board before writing

troubleshoots.fix: The session cookie expired; log in to Milanote in the browser and re-run auth login --cookie
Load-balancer stickiness was lost; retry the command (the client re-handshakes with a fresh cookie jar)

troubleshoots.symptom: Writes rejected on a free account
troubleshoots.fix: Free plans stop at 100 cards; run usage to see the count

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when an agent needs to read, build or reorganize Milanote boards: pushing a Markdown outline onto a board as headings, notes and checklists, tidying a board onto an even grid, uploading a folder of storyboard frames, or reading a board tree back as text.
anti_triggers: Drawing sketches or editing images inside Milanote
Real-time collaboration or watching other people's cursors
Accounts you are not logged in to in a browser
